output_quality_evals.name: grounded-in-actual-guesses
output_quality_evals.prompt: Write up what we did on the export project.
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Deliverable produced, then 2-4 coaching points naming actual guesses made (audience, format, depth). Each quotes the phrase, states the assumption, supplies the rewording. No generic advice.

output_quality_evals.name: clear-request-no-coaching
output_quality_evals.prompt: Add a function to src/parse.py called parse_iso_date that takes a string, returns a datetime in UTC, and raises ValueError on anything that isn't ISO-8601. Tests in tests/test_parse.py, pytest style, cover the error path.
output_quality_evals.expected_output: No coaching section at all. The request determined every choice. Manufacturing feedback here teaches the user to skip it.

output_quality_evals.name: blocking-ambiguity-asked-not-coached
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Asks during the work rather than guessing and coaching afterward. Coaching is for reasonable assumptions, not for questions that should have been raised.

output_quality_evals.name: casual-request-proportionate
output_quality_evals.prompt: can you tidy up this function a bit
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Light touch or no coaching. Does not demand acceptance criteria for a small casual ask. Over-formalizing makes users write less, not more.

output_quality_evals.name: recurring-pattern-raised-once
output_quality_evals.prompt: [Fourth task in a sequence where audience was ambiguous each time] Draft the summary for this.
output_quality_evals.expected_output: Raises the recurring pattern once, as a pattern, rather than repeating the per-task note a fourth time.

output_quality_evals.name: user-declines-feedback
output_quality_evals.prompt: [User previously said they don't want the prompt feedback] Write the migration script.
output_quality_evals.expected_output: No coaching section. The preference is honored without negotiation or a reminder that it is available.

trigger_evals.query: write up what we did on the export project
that's not what i meant at all. why did you build it that way?
we keep going back and forth on these - how could i be phrasing my asks better so you get it right first time
make the dashboard better and let me know if my request was clear enough
build the retry logic for the payment worker, then tell me where i was vague
what's the best way to write prompts for claude generally? any guides?
review this requirements doc and tell me which requirements are ambiguous
critique my writing style in this email draft
add a created_at column to the orders table migration, postgres, default now()
teach me prompt engineering techniques for our team training deck

notes: Output evals #2, #4 and #6 are the restraint guards: coaching on a clear request, over-formalizing a casual one, or ignoring a stated preference all destroy the practice faster than missing a coaching opportunity. Eval #3 enforces the boundary that blocking ambiguity gets a question during the work, not feedback afterward. The near-miss negative worth watching is spec review, which is a different skill operating on the same vocabulary.
